title: Meet Ellie the Elephant
author: Shellfie original
credit: An original story written for Shellfie.

pages: Meet Ellie the Elephant! Ellie is a baby African elephant. She lives on the savanna, where the grass is tall and the sun is hot.
Ellie lives in a herd with her mom, her aunts, and her cousins. The leader of the herd is Ellie's grandma. She is the oldest and wisest of them all.
Elephants eat plants all day long. They eat grass, leaves, roots, fruit, and even tree bark. A grown-up elephant can eat more than 300 pounds of food in one day!
Ellie's trunk is her nose and her top lip together. She uses it to smell, to grab, to drink, and to give hugs.
But Ellie's trunk is still wobbly. Yesterday she tried to take a drink, and she sprayed water right up her own nose. AH-CHOO!
On hot days, Ellie rolls in the mud. Mud is like sunscreen and bug spray for elephants. Ellie thinks it is the best part of the day.
Lions sometimes watch the herd. They hope to find a baby who wanders away. When the grown-ups see a lion, they make a circle around the babies and trumpet loudly. The lions give up and leave.
Elephants talk with low rumbles. Some rumbles are so low that people can not hear them, but other elephants can feel them through their feet!
At night, Ellie sleeps close to her mom. Elephants can live for sixty years or more, and they remember their friends for a very long time.

quiz.q: Who is the leader of Ellie's herd?
quiz.ev: The leader of the herd is Ellie's grandma.

quiz.q: Why do the grown-ups make a circle around the babies?
o: To keep them safe from lions
